title: Standardize WebView color semantics
summary: Audits and standardizes WebView UI color semantics through CSS tokens, class usage, and drift-prevention tests.
reason: The WebView uses status, evidence, advisory, selected, disabled, and panel colors across many pages; consistent semantic tokens prevent the same color from implying conflicting operator states.
behavior_before: Several WebView state colors and panel tones were locally defined or overloaded, making success, warning, danger, pending, evidence, advisory, selection, and panel intent harder to distinguish consistently across pages.
behavior_after: WebView CSS uses a canonical semantic token map for state, evidence, advisory, selection, disabled, and panel intent colors while preserving backend-owned text, routes, commands, settings persistence, and media/file authority.
